whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the CPQ Administrator exam for?

personas.label: Admins who have inherited a CPQ org
personas.description: CPQ was implemented by a partner and now you maintain it. This is the ground you need to cover to work on it safely.

personas.label: Revenue operations people
personas.description: You own quoting and renewals as a process and need to know what the tool can and cannot be made to do.

personas.label: Consultants moving into quote-to-cash
personas.description: Core Salesforce skills transfer less here than you would expect. CPQ has its own data model and its own rule engine.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the CPQ Administrator Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: One of the harder Salesforce exams, and not because the questions are tricky. CPQ is a managed package with its own data model, its own pricing sequence and its own rule engine, and almost none of it follows from general admin experience. The passing score is the usual 65%, but the volume of product-specific detail is what makes it hard.
bullets: 60 questions in 105 minutes. Most questions are a quoting requirement with four plausible configurations.
Around 65% to pass. Standard threshold, unusually dense subject matter.
Product rules and price rules get confused constantly. Product rules decide what can be on the quote. Price rules change values on the quote lines.
The pricing sequence is examinable in order. List, special, regular, customer, net, and what each stage can alter.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: The honest test is whether you have built one. Configure a bundle with options and constraints, add a discount schedule. Write a price rule that fires on the Quote Line Editor, contract the quote and then run a renewal and an amendment. If you have not done that cycle end to end at least once, reading about it will not be enough.

examFormat.heading: CPQ Administrator Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: Proctored online or at a test centre. The shape of it:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Most of the exam is scenario work. A business wants tiered discounting, or a bundle where choosing one option excludes another, or a mid-term upgrade prorated correctly, and you have to name the CPQ mechanism that does it.
bestWayToPass: Get a developer org with CPQ installed and build in it. There is no substitute. The Quote Line Editor behaves in ways no description prepares you for.

Draw the pricing waterfall out by hand. List, special, regular, customer, net. Then place discount schedules, block prices, contracted prices and price rules on it. Many questions are answerable from that one diagram.
Learn the rule types by what they touch. Product rules evaluate and act on product selection, validation and alerts. Price rules write to fields. Once that is firm, most rule questions resolve.

Follow one deal through the whole lifecycle. Quote to order to contract to subscription to renewal to amendment. Renewals and amendments are a reliable source of questions and are the part people skip.

certificationCard.description: Covers configuring Salesforce CPQ end to end: bundles and product options, product and price rules, the pricing waterfall, discount schedules and approvals, quote documents, and the contract lifecycle through renewals and amendments.

keyConcepts.h2: CPQ Administrator: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Product Rules Versus Price Rules
blocks.body: This distinction is the single most important thing on the exam. Product rules act on what is allowed to be on a quote. They come in four types: validation rules block a quote that breaks a condition, selection rules add, remove, enable or disable options automatically, alert rules warn without blocking, and filter rules restrict what the product search returns. They are driven by error conditions and actions, and they mostly fire in the configurator. Price rules act on field values. They have conditions and then price actions that write a value, a formula or a field reference into a target field on the quote line or the quote. The things to hold on to are the evaluation events, which decide when a rule runs: On Initialization, Before Calculate, On Calculate and After Calculate. If a question describes something that stops a quote, think product rule. If it describes something that changes a number, think price rule.

blocks.heading: Bundles, Features and Options
blocks.body: A bundle is a parent product with product options attached, usually grouped into features. Features carry the min and max option counts, which is how you enforce rules like choose exactly one platform and up to three add-ons. Options carry their own quantity, bundled flag and selection defaults, and a bundled option is priced inside the parent rather than separately, which is why its price does not appear on its own quote line. Configuration attributes sit at the top of the configurator and let a user pick once, for example a region or a tier, and have that selection drive the options beneath through selection rules. Nested bundles are allowed, an option that is itself a bundle, and the exam expects you to know that the configurator walks down into them. The common scenario is a constraint such as choosing option A must disable option B, and the answer is a selection rule with the appropriate action.

blocks.heading: The Pricing Waterfall
blocks.body: CPQ prices a line in a fixed sequence and each stage can only be influenced by particular mechanisms. List price comes from the price book entry. Special price is where block pricing, contracted prices and subscription pricing apply. Regular price is the special price adjusted for quantity-based pricing. Customer price is regular price after discounts, which is where discount schedules and manual discounts land. Net price is customer price after any partner and distributor discounts. Knowing the order matters because a question will tell you a discount is not being applied as expected, and the reason is usually that something earlier in the sequence has already fixed the value. Discount schedules themselves come in two shapes: slab, where each tier applies only to the units inside it, and range, where the tier reached applies to all units. Questions test that difference with numbers.

blocks.heading: Discounts, Contracted Prices and Approvals
blocks.body: Discounting in CPQ comes from several places and they stack in a defined way. Discount schedules apply automatically by volume or term. Contracted prices hold a negotiated price for a specific account and product, and they apply at the special price stage, which means they override list price for that customer on every future quote. Manual discounts are entered by the sales user on the line and can be capped by the discount fields on the product or by approvals. Approvals are where CPQ departs from core Salesforce: advanced approvals is a separate package feature with approval chains, smart approvals that skip approvers who have already approved an equal or larger discount, and approval rules based on quote or line conditions. If a question mentions parallel approvers or an approver being skipped on resubmission, it is about advanced approvals rather than standard approval processes.

blocks.heading: Contracts, Subscriptions, Renewals and Amendments
blocks.body: When a quote is ordered and contracted, CPQ creates a contract and turns subscription products into subscription records with start and end dates. Renewals are driven by the contract: renewal forecasting and renewal quoting flags determine whether CPQ creates the renewal opportunity and quote automatically as the end date approaches, and the renewal quote starts from the current subscriptions rather than from scratch. Amendments handle change inside the term. An amendment quote shows the existing subscriptions and lets you add, remove or change quantity, and CPQ prorates the difference across the remaining term, which is why the amount on an amendment is rarely the full list price. Two details earn marks: an amendment is always made against the contract rather than the original quote, and the subscription term and the proration multiplier are what drive the prorated figures.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce CPQ Administrator Exam
scenarioTips.intro: CPQ scenarios describe a commercial requirement and expect you to name the configuration. Knowing which object or rule type owns each behaviour is most of the work.

blocks.heading: Rule Type by Effect
blocks.body: Blocks or changes the product selection, product rule. Writes a value into a field, price rule. Sort this out first and a quarter of the exam becomes easier.

blocks.heading: The Waterfall in Order
blocks.body: List, special, regular, customer, net. Know which mechanism acts at which stage, especially contracted prices at special and discount schedules at customer.

blocks.heading: Slab Versus Range Schedules
blocks.body: Range applies the reached tier to every unit. Slab applies each tier only to the units within it. Expect to be given quantities and prices.

blocks.heading: Advanced Approvals Vocabulary
blocks.body: Smart approvals, approval chains, parallel approvers. If these words appear, the answer is advanced approvals, not the standard approval process.

blocks.heading: Amendment Proration
blocks.body: Amendments work from the contract, show existing subscriptions, and prorate over the remaining term. Build one in an org and watch the numbers.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Certifications to Consider
nextCertsAfter.intro: Where CPQ admins commonly go next:

sampleQuestions.question: A bundle must prevent a user from selecting the Premium Support option when the Basic tier has been chosen. What should the admin configure?
options: A selection rule that disables the option
A validation rule on the Quote object
A price rule with a conditional action
sampleQuestions.explanation: Selection rules add, remove, enable or disable options in the configurator, which is exactly this requirement.
whyWrong: A validation rule would block the quote after the fact rather than preventing the selection.
Price rules change field values; they do not control option availability.
Discount schedules affect pricing, not option availability.

sampleQuestions.question: A negotiated price for one account on one product must apply automatically to all future quotes for that account. What should be used?
options: A new price book for the account
A manual discount on each quote
sampleQuestions.explanation: Contracted prices store an account-specific price for a product and apply at the special price stage on every quote.
whyWrong: A dedicated price book per account does not scale and is not the CPQ mechanism for this.
Discount schedules apply by volume or term, not by account.
Manual discounts rely on the user remembering, which is not automatic.

sampleQuestions.question: A discount schedule is configured so that reaching the 100-unit tier applies that tier's rate to all 100 units. Which type is this?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Range schedules apply the rate of the tier reached to the entire quantity.
whyWrong: Slab applies each tier's rate only to the units falling inside that tier.
Term discounts vary by subscription length, not quantity.
Block pricing sets a fixed total for a quantity band rather than a per-unit discount.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer wants to add 20 licences four months into a twelve-month contract. What should the admin do?
options: Create an entirely new quote on a new opportunity
Create an amendment quote from the contract
sampleQuestions.explanation: Amendments are made against the contract and prorate the change across the remaining term.
whyWrong: A separate new quote would not prorate against the existing term or link to the contract.
Renewals handle the next term, not a change inside the current one.
The original quote is closed once contracted and should not be edited.

sampleQuestions.question: At which stage of the pricing waterfall do discount schedules take effect?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Discounts, including schedules, are applied to produce the customer price.
whyWrong: Special price is where contracted prices and block pricing act.
Net price applies partner and distributor discounts after customer price.
List price comes straight from the price book entry before any adjustment.

sampleQuestions.question: Which evaluation event should a price rule use if it must set a field before CPQ performs its calculation?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Before Calculate runs ahead of the calculation so the value is in place when CPQ prices the line.
whyWrong: On Save is not one of the CPQ price rule evaluation events.
On Initialization runs when the editor opens, not around each calculation.
After Calculate runs once pricing is complete, which is too late to influence it.

sampleQuestions.question: A sales user must be warned that a configuration is unusual; but still allowed to proceed. Which product rule type fits?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Alert rules display a message without preventing the quote from continuing.
whyWrong: Validation rules block the quote, which the requirement explicitly does not want.
Selection rules change which options are chosen or available.
Filter rules restrict what the product search returns.

sampleQuestions.question: What happens to subscription products when a quote is ordered and contracted?
options: Subscription records with start and end dates
They are held until the renewal date
They are deleted from the quote
sampleQuestions.explanation: Contracting turns subscription quote lines into subscription records that drive renewals and amendments.
whyWrong: Subscriptions are created at contracting, not at renewal.
Quote lines remain as the record of what was sold.
Subscription products stay subscriptions; their pricing type does not change.

sampleQuestions.question: An approver who has already approved a 20% discount should not be asked again when the quote is resubmitted at 15%. Which feature does this?
options: A validation rule placed on the quote record
sampleQuestions.explanation: Smart approvals skip approvers who have already approved an equal or greater discount on resubmission.
whyWrong: Validation rules block records; they do not route approvals.
Standard Salesforce approval processes restart the chain on resubmission.
Alert rules display messages and are unrelated to approval routing.

sampleQuestions.question: A feature in a bundle must allow between one and three options to be selected. Where is this set?
options: The quantity field on each option
The min and max fields on the feature
sampleQuestions.explanation: Features carry the minimum and maximum option counts that constrain selection within them.
whyWrong: Option quantity controls how many of that option, not how many options.
Price book entries set pricing, not configuration limits.
A validation rule could catch a breach afterwards but the feature fields enforce it directly.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a bundled product option mean for pricing?
options: Its price sits in the parent, not on its own line
It is always free of charge
It must be discounted to zero manually
It appears as a separate quote line with its own total
sampleQuestions.explanation: Bundled options are priced within the parent product rather than contributing their own line total.
whyWrong: Bundled is about where the price sits, not whether the option has value.
No manual discounting is needed; the behaviour is built in.
A separately priced line is what an unbundled option produces.

sampleQuestions.question: A configuration attribute is placed at the top of a bundle configurator. What is it for?
options: Replacing the need for product rules
One selection that drives the options below
sampleQuestions.explanation: Configuration attributes let a user choose once, and selection rules then act on that choice across the bundle.
whyWrong: Attributes supply input to rules rather than replacing them.
Totals are calculated on the quote, not held in a configuration attribute.
Contract dates come from the contracting process.

sampleQuestions.question: A renewal opportunity and quote should be created automatically as a contract approaches its end date. What governs this?
options: The renewal forecasting and quoting settings
A scheduled Apex job written by the admin
A price rule with an After Calculate event
sampleQuestions.explanation: Those two contract flags are what tell CPQ to generate the renewal opportunity and quote.
whyWrong: Amendments handle change within the current term.
Custom code is unnecessary because the feature is standard.
Price rules affect field values on a quote, not renewal creation.

sampleQuestions.question: Why might a manual discount entered by a sales user fail to change the net price as expected?
options: An earlier stage has already fixed the value
Manual discounts are not supported in CPQ
Discounts only apply to subscription products
sampleQuestions.explanation: The waterfall runs in order, so a value set at an earlier stage can override what a later discount attempts.
whyWrong: Net price is the result of discounts, not immune to them.
Manual discounting is a standard CPQ capability.
Discounts apply to one-off products as well as subscriptions.

sampleQuestions.question: Which best describes what a filter rule does?
options: Restricts what the product search returns
Writes a value into a target field
Blocks a quote from being saved
sampleQuestions.explanation: Filter rules narrow the product selection a user can search, based on conditions.
whyWrong: Writing field values is what price actions do.
Blocking a save is the job of a validation rule.
Proration is part of the amendment calculation, not a rule type.
